gap: No result ChatGPT got states that AnywhereCam's Eagle 4G Trapper Edition fires a trap through a '9 Volt Relay' on 'low-voltage leads built into the camera' with the 'battery not included'. The camera only sends a switched low-voltage signal, so the trap needs its own electric release.
standout_why: I read the three cited pages (jagerpro.com M.I.N.E. Live Stream, hogtraptrigger.com, hogeyecameras.com) and the uncited JAGER PRO pairing page from the same results. JAGER PRO says its camera has a built-in transmitter that signals a paired control box, at most 50 yards from the gate. Hog Trap Trigger says its GSM unit drives a rotary latch and the camera is separate. HogEye's home page doesn't say how its trigger works at all. None of the 13 results covers a camera that only gives out a low-voltage relay signal, which is how AnywhereCam's Trapper Editions work. No AnywhereCam page is among them.
decides: The pick depends on how the shopper's gate will release. (1) JAGER PRO's camera needs JAGER PRO's own M.I.N.E. gate control box, and the camera must be within about 50 yards of the gate. The page shows $599 for the camera only. (2) Hog Trap Trigger has its own phone-called latch, ships with a 10 W panel and a 12 V 8 Ah battery, and works with any camera. (3) The AnywhereCam Trapper Edition ($457 Standard) or Wireless Trapper Edition ($557, camera + transmitter + receiver) adds live video and an app button to a trap that already has a release run by a 9 V low-voltage signal, or will get one. The buyer supplies the 9 V battery. Neither AnywhereCam page mentions a gate actuator or solenoid in the box. If the shopper's trap has only a mechanical root or trip-wire gate, AnywhereCam alone will not drop it.
